title: Looping Through Python Lists
learningObjectives: Explain the behavior of looping through python lists.
Select appropriate list operations for a given task.
Predict the effect of indexing, mutation and copying.
Write readable code that processes list data.
Avoid common list-related errors and side effects.

understand.concept: A for loop can visit each list item directly. enumerate provides both an index and item. A while loop can also process list positions using an index and a length check. Avoid changing a list's size while iterating over it unless the behavior is intentional and understood.
understand.whyItMatters: Looping through lists is a core pattern for filtering, transforming, counting and summarizing collections.
understand.analogy: It is like inspecting each card in a stack and recording information about it.
understand.analogyLimit: Direct iteration is usually clearer than index-based iteration when the index is not needed; enumerate is useful when both are required.

explain.narrative:
## 1. Direct iteration

Use `for item in items:` when you need each value.

## 2. Index and item together

Use `enumerate(items)` to receive pairs of index and value.

## 3. Index-based while loop

Use a counter with `len(items)` when index-based control is necessary.

## 4. Avoid unsafe mutation

Removing items from a list while iterating can cause elements to be skipped. Build a new list or iterate over a copy when appropriate.

examples.title: Print each item
examples.explanation: Direct iteration provides each item without manual indexing.

examples.title: Use enumerate for index and item
examples.explanation: enumerate yields an index and corresponding item for each iteration.

examples.title: Start enumerate at one
examples.explanation: The start parameter changes the first index supplied by enumerate.

examples.title: Loop with a while index
examples.code:
values = [5, 10, 15]
index = 0
while index < len(values):
    print(values[index])
    index += 1
examples.explanation: The index advances until it reaches the list length.

examples.title: Build a filtered list
examples.explanation: The loop creates a separate list containing only even values.

practise.guidedTask: Loop over a list of names and print each name with a one-based number using enumerate.
practise.independentTask: Given a list of numbers, build a new list containing only values above a chosen threshold. Do not remove items from the list being iterated.
hints: Use direct for iteration when you only need values.
Use enumerate when you need index and value.
enumerate can start counting at one.
A while loop needs an index update.
Avoid removing list items during direct iteration.
practise.challenge: Demonstrate how removing items during iteration can skip values. Rewrite the code using a filtered new list.

questions.prompt: Which construct provides both index and value?
questions.explanation: enumerate yields an index and the corresponding item.

questions.prompt: What is the default starting index of enumerate?
questions.explanation: enumerate starts at zero unless start is specified.

questions.prompt: When is direct list iteration best?
options: When only each item is needed
When the list must be sorted
When every item must be deleted
questions.answer: When only each item is needed
questions.explanation: Direct iteration avoids unnecessary manual index management.

questions.prompt: Why can removing items while iterating be risky?
questions.explanation: Removing shifts later indexes while the iterator advances.

questions.prompt: How can a new filtered list be built?
options: Append selected items to a separate list
Delete the original list each iteration
Change the list into a dictionary
questions.answer: Append selected items to a separate list
questions.explanation: A separate result list avoids mutating the collection being traversed.
